unit.title: Season Now
unit.summary: This week in pickleball: current events, draws, rankings, standings, news and seasonal changes.

lessons.title: This week in pickleball
lessons.objective: Know what's on this week and why it matters.

payload.prompt: Why do pro pickleball fans check the schedule every week?

options.text: To find out which tours have events and who's playing.
To buy tickets for their favorite player.
To predict who will win.
To check the weather.

explanation.correct: Schedules show what's happening this week across tours and help you follow the action.
explanation.incorrect: Checking the schedule tells you which events are live and which players are competing.
explanation.sayThisLine: Events change week to week. That's why the schedule matters.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: Huge week for pickleball. Ben's playing and there's an MLP event.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: Multiple important events are happening at the same time.
She only cares about one player.
The weather will be big.
She's tired of pickleball.

payload.translation: When multiple events or favorite players are competing at once, it's a big week to follow.

followUps.line: Big weeks mean more to watch and more to talk about.
followUps.why: Explains why it matters to her.

followUps.line: She's signaling that this week has something special.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Fans track schedules to catch their favorite players and events.

payload.prompt: This week's schedule tells you everything you need to know about pickleball right now. True?

choices.label: No, rankings and news matter too

explanation.correct: The schedule shows what's happening, but rankings, news and standings add meaning.
explanation.incorrect: Schedules matter, but context (who's hot, rule changes, standings) makes them meaningful.
explanation.sayThisLine: Schedule tells you what; rankings and news tell you why it matters.

payload.prompt: She's watching her favorite pro this week. What should you do?

situation.narrative: Your person is excited about a match happening this week.

facts.label: What she said
facts.value: Going to stream Ben's match Thursday night.

facts.label: What you know
facts.value: You know the tours are happening; you can ask about it.

options.label: Ask to watch it with her
options.consequence: Perfect. You show interest and get to learn by watching together.
considerations: It's a natural way to follow along

options.label: Say 'good luck' and leave it
options.consequence: Kind, but you miss a chance to engage with what she loves.

payload.expertNote: Being curious about who's playing and when creates natural conversation.

payload.prompt: Complete the schedule sentence.
payload.template: This week {{tour}} is hosting an event and {{player}} is playing in it.

explanation.correct: Pro schedules tell you which tour events and which pros are competing.
explanation.incorrect: Following schedules means tracking tour events and who's playing in them.
explanation.sayThisLine: Schedule = tour + players this week. That's how you stay current.

lessons.title: Read the draw
lessons.objective: Follow the current event's bracket and seeding.

payload.prompt: What does reading a draw tell you?

options.text: Who plays whom and in what order; top seeds get favorable matchups early.
How much money the winner gets.
Which paddle brand most pros use.
The weather forecast for the tournament.

explanation.correct: A draw shows the bracket, seeding and matchup pairings for the event.
explanation.incorrect: Reading a draw tells you the structure: who faces whom and when.
explanation.sayThisLine: Draw shows the bracket. Top seeds avoid each other early.

payload.prompt: In a tournament bracket, where are the top seeds positioned?

diagram.alt: Tournament bracket with top seeds placed in opposite halves to avoid meeting early.

explanation.correct: You identified the correct positioning.
explanation.incorrect: That is not where top seeds are placed to create strong finals.

payload.prompt: The draw is released before the tournament starts. True?

explanation.correct: Draws are published before the event so players can plan and fans can preview matchups.
explanation.incorrect: The draw comes out beforehand so fans can follow the storyline.
explanation.sayThisLine: Draw release = hype. That's when fans start the bracket talk.

payload.prompt: Match draw and bracket terms.

pairs.definition: A player's seeding rank (1, 2, 3, etc.) based on ranking; top seeds get favorable draw placement.
The published bracket showing who plays whom and the match order.
A free pass to the next round (top seeds get byes in early rounds).

explanation.summary: Seed = rank; draw = bracket; bye = skipping a round.
explanation.sayThisLine: Top seeds get byes and easier early draws.

payload.prompt: Complete the draw statement.
payload.template: When the draw is released, {{player}} is a {{seed}} seed, so {{advantage}}.

options: she gets an easier path early
she has to play the hardest opponents
gaps.correct: she gets an easier path early

explanation.correct: Top seeds are positioned to avoid strong opponents until later rounds.
explanation.incorrect: Better seeding means a better bracket draw and an easier early path.
explanation.sayThisLine: Top seed = easier draw. That's why seeding matters.

lessons.title: Rankings movers
lessons.objective: Interpret who moved in the world rankings and why.

payload.prompt: What causes a player's world ranking to jump up?

options.text: Winning a big event and earning ranking points.
Being popular on social media.
Having the best paddle.
Playing the most matches.

explanation.correct: Tournament wins and points earned directly improve a player's ranking.
explanation.incorrect: Rankings move because of tournament results and the points you earned.
explanation.sayThisLine: Win a slam, your ranking jumps. That's how rankings work.

payload.prompt: How many positions might a player move after winning a major event? (1 = 1 spot, 100 = 100 spots)

explanation.correct: A big win typically moves a player 10-30 spots up, depending on their current rank.
explanation.incorrect: Major events award large point swings that move rankings significantly.
explanation.sayThisLine: Win a slam, expect a big ranking jump. Sometimes 20+ spots.

payload.prompt: A player who hasn't won recently might drop in the rankings. True?

explanation.correct: Rankings can decay if a player hasn't earned points recently or loses matches.
explanation.incorrect: Rankings are live; they move as players earn or lose points.
explanation.sayThisLine: Take time off, your ranking drops. That's how rankings stay current.

payload.prompt: Your person's favorite player just moved up 15 spots. What happened?

situation.narrative: A ranking jump usually means something good.

options.label: They won or did very well in a recent event
options.consequence: Correct. A ranking jump means recent success and points earned.

options.label: They took a break and relaxed
options.consequence: No, a break drops rankings. This is good news.

payload.expertNote: Upward ranking movement signals recent tournament success.

payload.prompt: Complete the ranking statement.
payload.template: When a player's ranking jumps, it usually means they {{action}} and earned {{what}}.

explanation.correct: Tournament wins earn points that move rankings up.
explanation.incorrect: Ranking jumps come from recent tournament success.
explanation.sayThisLine: Jump in ranking = recent win. Ask her about the event.

lessons.title: MLP standings
lessons.objective: Read the current MLP table and playoff picture.

payload.prompt: What do MLP standings show you?

options.text: How many wins and losses each team has and their playoff position.
How many individual players are on each team.
Which paddle brand each team uses.
The age of each team's players.

explanation.correct: Standings show wins, losses, win percentage and playoff seeding.
explanation.incorrect: MLP standings rank teams by their record and show who's in playoff position.
explanation.sayThisLine: Standings tell you where your team stands in the race.

payload.title: Standings watch
payload.setting: Sam's team is in a playoff race.

exchanges.theirMessage: We're fourth but two games back. Still in it!

replies.text: Two games back with how many left to play?
replies.theirResponse: Five left. We can make it up.
replies.coachNote: Showed you understood standings and asked a practical question.

replies.theirResponse: Yeah, barely. Hoping we can climb.
replies.coachNote: Kind but general. Ask about the path to playoffs.

replies.text: You'll never make playoffs from fourth.
replies.coachNote: You discouraged her. Standings are fluid; games left matter.

payload.closingNote: In MLP, teams climb the standings by winning matches. Being a few games back with games left is still very much in play.

payload.prompt: A team at 8-3 is definitely in the playoff picture. True?

explanation.correct: A record's strength depends on how many games remain and how close teams are.
explanation.incorrect: Good records help, but where you stand relative to other teams matters more.
explanation.sayThisLine: Your record matters less than your position and games left.

payload.prompt: Order the MLP season arc.

items.text: Teams jockey for playoff position (late July)

explanation.sayThisLine: Season starts, teams climb the standings, playoffs decide the champion.
explanation.correct: MLP seasons flow from opening through playoffs to a final champion.
explanation.incorrect: The regular season builds standings, then playoffs are the climax.

payload.prompt: Complete the standings statement.
payload.template: In MLP, the standings change {{frequency}} because {{reason}}.

options: wins and losses move teams up and down
gaps.correct: wins and losses move teams up and down

explanation.correct: Weekly matches change the standings as teams earn wins and losses.
explanation.incorrect: Standings are live and change after every match result.
explanation.sayThisLine: Every week, results reshuffle the standings.

lessons.title: The news explainer
lessons.objective: Understand why a pickleball headline is a big deal.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: Did you hear? The spin test starts next month. My paddle might get banned.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: A new rule tests paddles to make sure they're fair; if hers is too spinny, it might not be approved.
She's going to spin a paddle and fail a fitness test.
All paddles are being destroyed.
She's being dramatic about nothing.

payload.translation: Equipment regulations change. When they do, some gear has to be re-tested or might not meet new rules.

followUps.line: New equipment rules can affect what gear people use.
followUps.why: Shows you understand it's a bigger issue.

followUps.line: Ask her if she's looking to buy a backup paddle.
followUps.why: Practical follow-up that shows you listened.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Rule and equipment changes are normal and create gear-talk opportunities.

payload.prompt: Why do pickleball fans care about rule changes?

options.text: Rules change the game they play or watch and affect strategy.
They like to complain about everything.
Rules don't matter; people just talk about them.
Rules are boring and nobody cares.

explanation.correct: Rule changes affect how the game is played and what strategy works.
explanation.incorrect: New rules matter because they reshape how people play and watch.
explanation.sayThisLine: Rule changes = new game. That's why fans care.

payload.prompt: Equipment news like paddle approvals and spin tests affect recreational players. True?

explanation.correct: USA Pickleball rules apply to all sanctioned play, including rec tournaments.
explanation.incorrect: When rules change, everyone playing organized pickleball is affected.
explanation.sayThisLine: Rule changes affect pros and rec players alike.

payload.prompt: She mentions a rule change you don't understand. What do you do?

situation.narrative: Rule talk can be confusing if you're new.

facts.label: What she said
facts.value: Something about the serve rules got tighter.

options.label: Ask her to explain what tightened
options.consequence: Perfect. She gets to teach you and feels heard.

options.label: Nod and change the subject
options.consequence: Safe, but you miss learning and showing interest.

payload.expertNote: Asking about rule changes is a natural way to learn and show interest.

payload.prompt: Complete the news statement.
payload.template: When there's a rule or equipment change, {{person}} usually {{action}}.

explanation.correct: Rule changes spark fan discussion and debate.
explanation.incorrect: When rules or gear change, it's natural fan-talk material.
explanation.sayThisLine: Change = debate. Debates = conversation. Listen and ask.

lessons.title: New season primer
lessons.objective: Reset for a new season or major rulebook update.

payload.prompt: When does the pickleball pro season typically reset?

options.text: August/September for PPA; May for MLP. Rankings reset with each new season.
Never; rankings carry over from year to year.
Randomly throughout the year.
Only when a major rule changes.

explanation.correct: Pro seasons have defined windows and rankings reset at season start.
explanation.incorrect: Each season brings new rankings, new schedules and fresh competition.
explanation.sayThisLine: Season starts = reset rankings. New tour season = new race.

payload.prompt: Order the year in pickleball.

items.text: Rankings and schedules are updated for the new season

explanation.sayThisLine: PPA late summer to spring. MLP late spring to summer. Overlaps happen.
explanation.correct: The pro year cycles through two main tours with different seasons.
explanation.incorrect: Tours have their own calendars; both run on annual cycles.

payload.prompt: A new season means everyone's ranking goes to zero. True?

choices.label: No, top players get seeded higher

explanation.correct: New seasons reset ranking points but seed top players higher in early events.
explanation.incorrect: While rankings reset, past performance influences seeding and early draw position.
explanation.sayThisLine: Rankings reset but top players still get respect in early seeding.

payload.prompt: A major rule change comes in January. What's the conversation about?

situation.narrative: Rule changes are frequent in pickleball.

facts.label: What happened
facts.value: USA Pickleball updated the serve rule clarity.

facts.label: What that means
facts.value: Players and fans debate how it changes the game.

options.label: People debate how it affects play and strategy
options.consequence: Correct. Rule changes spark fan analysis of impact.

options.label: Nobody talks about it; it's not important
options.consequence: No, rule changes are major topics in the community.

payload.expertNote: Rule changes are always fan-discussion material. Debates about impact are natural.

payload.prompt: Complete the season statement.
payload.template: At season start, the {{item}} is reset or updated for everyone.

explanation.correct: New seasons bring updated calendars, fresh rankings and often new or clarified rules.
explanation.incorrect: Season rollover means fresh starts for schedules, rankings and rule clarity.
explanation.sayThisLine: New season = new calendar, new rankings, same game.
